name: is_event_type_allowed
prose: Precondition: event_type is in [0, 64) so that BIT(event_type) is defined. Postcondition: for rsc_type MLX5_EVENT_QUEUE_TYPE_QP (0) it returns whether BIT(event_type) is in the set {PATH_MIG 0x01, COMM_EST 0x02, SQ_DRAINED 0x03, WQ_CATAS_ERROR 0x05, PATH_MIG_FAILED 0x07, WQ_INVAL_REQ_ERROR 0x10, WQ_ACCESS_ERROR 0x11, SRQ_LAST_WQE 0x13}; for MLX5_EVENT_QUEUE_TYPE_RQ (1) whether it is in {WQ_CATAS_ERROR 0x05, SRQ_LAST_WQE 0x13}; for MLX5_EVENT_QUEUE_TYPE_SQ (2) whether it is WQ_CATAS_ERROR (0x05); for MLX5_EVENT_QUEUE_TYPE_DCT (6) whether it is DCT_DRAINED (0x1c); for any other rsc_type it calls WARN and returns false. It has no other side effects.
note: reviewers right: the old prose had wrong sets (4 instead of 5 and 7) and DCT queue type 3 instead of 6 (mlx5 device.h:304-307, qpc.c:38-74). Contract dropped (WARN, and the old one encoded the wrong sets).

name: mlx5_ib_post_recv
prose: Precondition: ibqp is an mlx5 QP and wr is a list of receive work requests. Postcondition: it returns -EIO with *bad_wr = wr if the device is in internal error state and drain is false; for a GSI QP it returns mlx5_ib_gsi_post_recv(...) unchanged. Otherwise under qp->rq.lock (irqsave) it posts each request in order: it stops with -ENOMEM and *bad_wr = wr if the receive queue would overflow (mlx5r_wq_overflow), or -EINVAL and *bad_wr = wr if wr->num_sge exceeds qp->rq.max_gs; otherwise it writes the scatter entries (plus a terminating entry and signature segment when applicable) and records wr_id. At the end, if nreq requests were posted it advances qp->rq.head by nreq, issues wmb() and stores head & 0xffff in the doorbell record, then releases the lock and returns err (0 when all were posted, with earlier requests posted even on error).
note: slice cut the head; real function mlx5_ib_post_recv (mlx5/wr.c:1206-1284). Old drop only covered the tail.

name: mthca_process_mad
prose: Precondition: ibdev is an mthca device, in is a received MAD and out a writable MAD buffer; in_wc and in_grh may be NULL. Postcondition: for a locally generated trap (method IB_MGMT_METHOD_TRAP with slid 0) it calls forward_trap and returns IB_MAD_RESULT_SUCCESS | IB_MAD_RESULT_CONSUMED whether or not the forwarding worked. It returns IB_MAD_RESULT_SUCCESS (not handled here) for unsupported classes, methods (SM classes accept only GET, SET and TRAP_REPRESS; PMA and the vendor classes only GET and SET), SMInfo or vendor attributes of the SM classes, and when mthca_MAD_IFC returns -EBADMSG. It returns IB_MAD_RESULT_FAILURE (0) after logging when mthca_MAD_IFC fails with another error. After a successful MAD_IFC, if out->mad_hdr.status is 0 it calls smp_snoop and node_desc_override; for directed-route MADs it sets the return bit (1 << 15) in out's status; it returns IB_MAD_RESULT_SUCCESS | IB_MAD_RESULT_CONSUMED for a TRAP_REPRESS method and IB_MAD_RESULT_SUCCESS | IB_MAD_RESULT_REPLY otherwise. It takes no lock itself.
note: reviewer round 15 wrong: trap repress returns SUCCESS|CONSUMED (mthca_mad.c:193-195); old prose said FAILURE is 8, but IB_MAD_RESULT_FAILURE is 0 (ib_verbs.h:2227). Rounds 1-2 reflected.

name: mthca_alloc_db
prose: Precondition: dev->db_tab was initialised (memfree device) and db is writable. Postcondition: under dev->db_tab->mutex (released before return) it returns -EINVAL for an unsupported type. Types CQ_ARM and SQ use group 0 (pages searched upward from 0 to max_group1) and CQ_SET_CI, RQ and SRQ use group 1 (searched downward from npages - 1 to min_group2). It first looks for a page with a doorbell page allocated and a free record, then for a page slot without one, then, if max_group1 >= min_group2 - 1, returns -ENOMEM; otherwise it grows the group (++max_group1 or --min_group2, not undone later). For a new page it allocates a coherent DMA page (-ENOMEM on failure) and maps it with mthca_MAP_ICM_page, returning that function's error after freeing the buffer (page->db_rec is left pointing at the freed buffer). It then sets the first clear bit of the page's used bitmap; for group 1 the record index is MTHCA_DB_REC_PER_PAGE - 1 minus that bit, for group 0 it is the bit. It writes cpu_to_be64((qn << 8) | (type << 5)) into that record, stores a pointer to it in *db and returns page * MTHCA_DB_REC_PER_PAGE + record index. On error *db is unchanged.
note: reviewers rounds 1 and 15 right (the mapping error is returned as is, and for group 1 the set bit is not the returned index); round 2 right that success returns a positive index. mthca_memfree.c:569-640.

name: qedr_reg_user_mr
prose: Precondition: ibpd is a qedr PD. Postcondition: it returns ERR_PTR(-EOPNOTSUPP) if dmah is non-NULL and ERR_PTR(-EINVAL) if IB_ACCESS_REMOTE_WRITE is requested without IB_ACCESS_LOCAL_WRITE; ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM) if the mr allocation fails; then pins the memory with ib_umem_get (ERR_PTR(-EFAULT) on failure), builds the PBL with init_mr_info (its error on failure), allocates a TID with rdma_alloc_tid and registers it with rdma_register_tid (their errors returned). On success it returns &mr->ibmr with lkey = itid << 8 | key and rkey set the same way only when remote read, write or atomic access was requested. On failure after the mr allocation it frees the PBL, frees the TID if it was registered-stage, and frees mr, but it never calls ib_umem_release on mr->umem, so the pinned memory reference is not released by this function.
note: reviewer round 1 right (umem is not released on failure paths, qedr/verbs.c:2955-3003); round 2 wrong (the old prose already described the dmah and access checks); round 15's free_pbl_list claim not verifiable here and not asserted.

name: usnic_ib_qp_grp_modify
prose: Precondition: qp_grp is a valid usnic_ib_qp_grp, the caller does not hold qp_grp->lock, new_state is an ib_qp_state and data is NULL or a usnic_transport_spec. Postcondition: it reads old_state before taking qp_grp->lock (spin_lock), performs the transition under the lock and releases it, and returns the status. RESET: from RESET nothing; from INIT it releases and removes all flows; from RTR, RTS or ERR it disables the group and releases all flows; other old states give -EINVAL. INIT: from RESET it creates and adds a flow if data is given (error from create_and_add_flow or -EFAULT when it returns NULL), none otherwise; from INIT it does the same but -EINVAL when data is NULL; from RTR or RTS it disables the group; other old states -EINVAL. RTR: only from INIT, enabling the group (-EINVAL otherwise). RTS: only from RTR, a no-op. ERR: from RESET it calls the QP event handler with IB_EVENT_QP_FATAL; from INIT it releases all flows then calls the handler; from RTR or RTS it disables the group, releases all flows and calls the handler (also when disabling fails); from ERR or other states -EINVAL. Any other new_state gives -EINVAL. After unlocking, if status is 0 it sets qp_grp->state to new_state and logs; otherwise it logs a failure and leaves state unchanged.
note: reviewer round 15 wrong, round 2 right: qp_grp->state = new_state is assigned after the lock is released when status == 0 (usnic_ib_qp_grp.c:538-540). Removed the unverifiable 'no leak' claim.

name: usnic_transport_rsrv_port
prose: Precondition: roce_bitmap was allocated by usnic_transport_init. Postcondition: if type is not USNIC_TRANSPORT_ROCE_CUSTOM it logs an error and returns 0 without taking roce_bitmap_lock or changing anything. For USNIC_TRANSPORT_ROCE_CUSTOM it takes roce_bitmap_lock; with a nonzero port_num whose bit is already set it logs an error, unlocks and returns 0; with a nonzero free port_num it sets its bit, unlocks and returns port_num; with port_num 0 it searches for a zero bit starting at roce_next_port with bitmap_find_next_zero_area, sets roce_next_port to (port_num & 4095) + 1, sets that bit, unlocks and returns it; if no free bit exists the search returns a value at or beyond ROCE_BITMAP_SZ, which is then set in the bitmap and returned (an out-of-range index). The lock is released on every path that took it.
note: reviewers rounds 2 and 15 right in part: the unsupported-type path returns without locking, and the no-free-port case does not return 0 (usnic_transport.c:80-97). 'Always releases the lock' replaced by a statement about paths that take it.

name: pvrdma_query_qp
prose: Precondition: ibqp is a pvrdma QP; attr and init_attr are writable. Postcondition: it takes qp->mutex. If qp->state is IB_QPS_RESET it sets attr->qp_state to IB_QPS_RESET and sends no command. Otherwise it posts PVRDMA_CMD_QUERY_QP; if pvrdma_cmd_post returns a negative value it logs and returns that value (attr is not filled from a response). On success it copies the response into attr, sets qp->state to attr->qp_state, and returns 0. In every case it then sets attr->cur_qp_state = attr->qp_state, fills init_attr from the QP, unlocks qp->mutex and returns the status.
note: slice cut the head; real function pvrdma_query_qp (pvrdma_qp.c:957-1046); the dropped item described only the tail.

name: pvrdma_post_send
prose: Precondition: ibqp is a pvrdma QP and wr is a list of send work requests. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL with *bad_wr = wr, without locking, if qp->state is below IB_QPS_RTS (RESET, INIT or RTR). Under qp->sq.lock it posts each request in order, stopping at the first failure with *bad_wr set: -ENOMEM if the send ring has no space; -EINVAL if num_sge is out of range, if the QP type is not UD or RC and the opcode is not IB_WR_SEND, if a UD/GSI request has an opcode other than SEND or SEND_WITH_IMM, if the opcode has no pvrdma mapping, if a UD/GSI request has no address handle, if the QP type is not GSI, UD or RC, or the negative result of set_reg_seg for IB_WR_REG_MR. A posted request has its header and SGEs written and sq.ring->prod_tail advanced. After unlocking, it rings the PVRDMA_UAR_QP_SEND doorbell only if all requests were posted and returns 0; on failure it returns the error without ringing the doorbell, although earlier requests of the same call remain in the ring.
note: reviewer round 15 wrong: the state check is qp->state < IB_QPS_RTS, i.e. RESET, INIT and RTR are rejected (pvrdma_qp.c:663-731). Slice cut the head. Old prose omitted the early failures and that earlier WRs stay queued.

name: rvt_modify_qp
prose: Precondition: ibqp is an rdmavt QP; the caller holds none of qp->r_lock, qp->s_hlock and qp->s_lock. Postcondition: it returns -EOPNOTSUPP immediately, before taking any lock, if attr_mask has bits outside IB_QP_ATTR_STANDARD_BITS. Otherwise it takes qp->r_lock (irq), s_hlock and s_lock and returns -EINVAL, with all three released and the QP unmodified, if ib_modify_qp_is_ok rejects the transition, the driver's check_modify_qp hook rejects it, or any requested attribute is invalid (AV or alternate AH dlid or rvt_check_ah, pkey indices, min_rnr_timer above 31, port, dest_qp_num, retry_cnt or rnr_retry above 7, path MTU, path migration state combinations, max_dest_rd_atomic, or SQE on an RC QP). Otherwise it applies the new state (RESET resets the QP, ERR calls rvt_error_qp and may flag a last-WQE event) and the masked attributes, calls the driver's modify_qp hook if any, releases the three locks, inserts the QP in the device table (rvt_insert_qp) when the transition is RESET to INIT, delivers IB_EVENT_QP_LAST_WQE_REACHED and IB_EVENT_PATH_MIG to the QP's event handler when applicable, and returns 0.
note: reviewer round 15 right: the -EOPNOTSUPP path returns before the locks are taken (rdmavt/qp.c:936-937), so 'releases all three on every path' was wrong. Slice cut the head (function starts at line 1389).

name: rvt_ruc_loopback
prose: Precondition: sqp is a valid loopback send QP whose port_num indexes rdi->ports; sqp->s_lock is not held on entry. The function takes the RCU read lock itself, looks up the responder QP with rvt_lookup_qpn(rdi, rvp, sqp->remote_qpn) (the result may be NULL), and takes and releases sqp->s_lock, qp->r_lock and sqp->r_lock itself. Postcondition: returns void; every exit path (labels unlock, clr_busy, done) drops the RCU read lock and the spin locks held at that point. If RVT_S_BUSY or any RVT_S_ANY_WAIT flag is already set in sqp->s_flags, or the sqp state lacks RVT_PROCESS_OR_FLUSH_SEND, it unlocks and returns without changing anything. Otherwise it sets RVT_S_BUSY and loops over send WQEs from sqp->s_last. The loop exits with RVT_S_BUSY cleared and s_lock released when s_last equals s_head, or when the sqp state allows neither processing nor flushing; if the state allows flushing but not processing, the WQE is completed with IB_WC_WR_FLUSH_ERR through rvt_send_complete and the loop continues. If the responder QP is missing, is not in a receive-ready state, or has a different QP type than sqp, the status is loopback_qp_drop(): rvp->n_pkt_drops is incremented and the status is IB_WC_RETRY_EXC_ERR for an RC sqp or IB_WC_SUCCESS otherwise; this path does not call rvt_rc_error and ends the loop. IB_WR_REG_MR and IB_WR_LOCAL_INV complete without touching the responder (LOCAL_INV calls rvt_invalidate_rkey unless RVT_SEND_COMPLETION_ONLY is set and uses IB_WC_LOC_PROT_ERR if that fails, without rvt_rc_error). SEND variants take a receive WQE with rvt_get_rwqe; RDMA WRITE, READ and the two atomics check access flags and rkey; on success data (or the atomic result) is moved, and if RVT_R_WRID_VALID was set a receive completion with IB_WC_SUCCESS is delivered to qp's CQ (not for atomics, REG_MR or LOCAL_INV). A successful WQE is completed with the computed send_status (IB_WC_SUCCESS on the normal path), rvp->n_loop_pkts is incremented, sqp->s_rnr_retry is reset to s_rnr_retry_cnt and the loop continues; local_ops_pending is decremented only on that send-completion/flush path and only after an IB_WR_LOCAL_INV that set local_ops. Error exits (each ends the loop): unsupported opcode -> IB_WC_LOC_QP_OP_ERR with no rvt_rc_error; rvt_get_rwqe < 0 -> IB_WC_REM_OP_ERR plus rvt_rc_error(qp, IB_WC_LOC_QP_OP_ERR); invalid request (flags, length, atomic alignment) -> IB_WC_REM_INV_REQ_ERR for RC but IB_WC_SUCCESS for non-RC with no data copied, plus rvt_rc_error(qp, IB_WC_LOC_QP_OP_ERR); rkey/access failure -> IB_WC_REM_ACCESS_ERR plus rvt_rc_error(qp, IB_WC_LOC_PROT_ERR). RNR NAK (no receive WQE): for UC the send WQE completes with IB_WC_SUCCESS and no data copied and the loop continues; for RC n_rnr_naks is incremented and, if s_rnr_retry is 0, the WQE is completed with IB_WC_RNR_RETRY_EXC_ERR without rvt_rc_error, otherwise s_rnr_retry is decremented (unless s_rnr_retry_cnt is 7), qp->r_lock is dropped, s_lock taken, rvt_add_rnr_timer is called only if the sqp state allows RVT_PROCESS_RECV_OK, RVT_S_BUSY is cleared and the function returns with no completion for that WQE. When an error exit completes the WQE: if sqp is RC it calls rvt_error_qp(sqp, IB_WC_WR_FLUSH_ERR) under sqp->r_lock, clears RVT_S_BUSY, releases s_lock and, if rvt_error_qp reported the last WQE, calls sqp's event handler with IB_EVENT_QP_LAST_WQE_REACHED; if sqp is not RC it clears RVT_S_BUSY and releases s_lock.
note: slice cut the head (real function starts at qp.c:2888). Reviewers: UC RNR NAK / non-RC inv_err completes with success and no copy: right (qp.c inv_err label, rnr_nak UC -> send_comp); unsupported opcode never calls rvt_rc_error and local_ops not decremented on error paths: right (default -> serr); RNR retry exhaustion jumps to serr without rvt_rc_error: right. Old prose also wrongly said the caller holds the RCU lock (rcu_read_lock is taken at function entry) and that rvt_rc_error is called on every error path except unsupported opcode (missing/not-ready responder and RNR exhaustion also skip it).

name: rvt_register_device
prose: Precondition: rdi may be NULL; otherwise it points to a driver-allocated rvt_dev_info. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL and does nothing else if rdi is NULL; returns -EINVAL (after pr_err) if check_support(rdi, i) is nonzero for any i below _VERB_IDX_MAX. Otherwise it sets rvt_dev_ops on rdi->ibdev and initializes mmap state, then calls rvt_driver_qp_init: if that fails it logs and returns -EINVAL (not the callee's error) and calls no exit function. It then initializes the AH lock and counter, calls rvt_driver_srq_init and rvt_driver_mcast_init (return values not used), and calls rvt_driver_mr_init: on failure it returns that error after rvt_qp_exit. It then calls rvt_wss_init: on failure it returns that error after rvt_mr_exit and rvt_qp_exit. It then initializes the CQ and PD locks and counter, ORs the POLL_CQ, REQ_NOTIFY_CQ, POST_SEND, POST_RECV and POST_SRQ_RECV bits into rdi->ibdev.uverbs_cmd_mask, sets node_type to RDMA_NODE_IB_CA and sets num_comp_vectors to 1 if it was 0. It then calls ib_register_device: on failure it returns that error after rvt_wss_exit, rvt_mr_exit and rvt_qp_exit. On success it calls rvt_create_mad_agents and returns 0. The returned error is the failing init or register call's own value (ret); the exit functions' results are not returned, and no undo is done for the AH, SRQ, multicast, CQ and PD setup.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (omits later failure returns such as ib_register_device) right, now enumerated; round 15 (cleanup omits ah/srq/mcast/cq/pd exits, cleanup functions are void so not returned) right: old prose said 'returns that function's value' for the cleanup calls. Old claim 'caller retaining ownership of rdi in all cases' removed (not tied to a line).

name: check_ack
prose: Precondition: qp, pkt and wqe point to valid structures with pkt->mask, pkt->opcode, pkt->psn, qp->comp.opcode, qp->comp.psn, wqe->wr.opcode, wqe->first_psn and wqe->last_psn set; for a response opcode that carries an AETH, pkt holds a valid AETH. Postcondition: returns an enum comp_state. First switch on qp->comp.opcode: for -1 it returns COMPST_ERROR if pkt->mask lacks RXE_START_MASK; for IB_OPCODE_RC_RDMA_READ_RESPONSE_FIRST or _MIDDLE it returns COMPST_ERROR when pkt->opcode is not IB_OPCODE_RC_ACKNOWLEDGE, _READ_RESPONSE_MIDDLE or _READ_RESPONSE_LAST and the packet is not a read retry (pkt->psn == wqe->first_psn with opcode _READ_RESPONSE_FIRST, or wqe->first_psn == wqe->last_psn with opcode _READ_RESPONSE_ONLY); any other qp->comp.opcode value issues WARN_ON_ONCE(1) and continues. Second switch on pkt->opcode: for _READ_RESPONSE_FIRST, _LAST or _ONLY it returns COMPST_ERROR if the AETH type is not AETH_ACK, returns COMPST_WRITE_SEND if wqe->wr.opcode is IB_WR_ATOMIC_WRITE, and otherwise falls through; for _READ_RESPONSE_MIDDLE (and the fall-through) it sets wqe->status = IB_WC_FATAL_ERR and returns COMPST_ERROR if wqe->wr.opcode is not IB_WR_RDMA_READ, IB_WR_RDMA_READ_WITH_INV or IB_WR_FLUSH, else calls reset_retry_counters(qp) and returns COMPST_READ. For IB_OPCODE_RC_ATOMIC_ACKNOWLEDGE it returns COMPST_ERROR if the AETH type is not AETH_ACK or wqe->wr.opcode is not IB_WR_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP or IB_WR_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD, else calls reset_retry_counters(qp) and returns COMPST_ATOMIC. For IB_OPCODE_RC_ACKNOWLEDGE: AETH_ACK calls reset_retry_counters(qp) and returns COMPST_WRITE_SEND; AETH_RNR_NAK increments RXE_CNT_RCV_RNR and returns COMPST_RNR_RETRY; an unknown AETH type returns COMPST_ERROR; AETH_NAK with syn AETH_NAK_PSN_SEQ_ERROR returns COMPST_ERROR_RETRY after, if psn_compare(pkt->psn, qp->comp.psn) > 0, incrementing RXE_CNT_RCV_SEQ_ERR, setting qp->comp.psn = pkt->psn and, if qp->req.wait_psn was nonzero, clearing it and setting qp->req.again = 1; AETH_NAK_INVALID_REQ sets wqe->status = IB_WC_REM_INV_REQ_ERR, AETH_NAK_REM_ACC_ERR sets IB_WC_REM_ACCESS_ERR, AETH_NAK_REM_OP_ERR sets IB_WC_REM_OP_ERR, any other NAK syn sets IB_WC_REM_OP_ERR after a debug message, and each returns COMPST_ERROR. Any other pkt->opcode logs a debug message and returns COMPST_ERROR.
note: Reviewers: round 1/2 (MIDDLE/LAST paths omitted or fall through to COMPST_ERROR): MIDDLE and LAST do not return COMPST_ERROR from the first switch and reach COMPST_READ unless wqe->wr.opcode is wrong (rxe_comp.c second switch cases FIRST/LAST/ONLY and MIDDLE); partly wrong, prose now enumerates it. Round 15 (WARN_ON_ONCE is in the second switch): wrong, WARN_ON_ONCE(1) is the default of the first switch (switch on qp->comp.opcode); the default of the second switch is a debug message followed by return COMPST_ERROR.

name: check_rkey
prose: Precondition: qp is a responder QP whose current request packet pkt has pkt->mask set; qp->resp holds state that qp_resp_from_reth or qp_resp_from_atmeth may overwrite (va, rkey, resid, length, offset). Postcondition: for read/write/atomic-write packets with RETH, flush packets with RETH, and atomic packets it first loads qp->resp fields from the RETH or ATMETH and derives the access flags; for a packet matching none of those masks it issues WARN_ON(1) and uses access 0 (there is no RESPST_ERR_MALFORMED_WQE return). Returns RESPST_EXECUTE with qp->resp.mr set to NULL when the packet is a read/write with RETH and reth_len is 0. Otherwise it looks up the MR: for an MW rkey via rxe_lookup_mw (a missing MW, or an MW whose mr is NULL, gives RESPST_ERR_RKEY_VIOLATION); a found MW takes a reference on its MR, sets qp->resp.offset to mw->addr if the MW is zero-based, and drops the MW reference; otherwise lookup_mr(qp->pd, ...) (NULL gives RESPST_ERR_RKEY_VIOLATION). Unless the packet is a FLUSH with selector IB_FLUSH_MR it returns RESPST_ERR_RKEY_VIOLATION if mr_check_range fails; an ATOMIC_WRITE packet returns RESPST_ERR_LENGTH unless resid and pktlen are both 8 and bth_pad is 0; a WRITE packet returns RESPST_ERR_LENGTH if resid > mtu and (pktlen != mtu or bth_pad != 0), or if resid <= mtu and (pktlen != resid or bth_pad != (0x3 & -resid)). On every error return qp->resp.mr is set to NULL and the references taken on the MR and MW in this call are dropped. On success it executes WARN_ON_ONCE(qp->resp.mr) if the field was already non-NULL, stores the MR (holding the reference taken by the lookup) in qp->resp.mr and returns RESPST_EXECUTE.
note: slice cut the head (real function at rxe_resp.c:449, outside slice 508-758). Reviewer (omits RESPST_ERR_MALFORMED_WQE for unsupported packet mask): wrong, no such return exists in check_rkey (the else branch at 'shouldn't happen' only does WARN_ON(1)); the old prose also missed the RESPST_ERR_LENGTH return details and the precondition on qp->resp.mr was misstated (only the final store warns).

name: siw_connect
prose: Precondition: id and params are valid pointers; params->qpn is looked up by the function. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL if params->private_data_len exceeds MPA_MAX_PRIVDATA; -ENOMEM if params->ird or params->ord exceeds sdev->attrs.max_ird or max_ord; -EAFNOSUPPORT if id->local_addr's family is neither AF_INET nor AF_INET6; all of these before any resource is taken. Then siw_qp_id2obj looks up the QP (taking a reference): if it fails, WARN and return -EINVAL. It then calls sock_create, kernel_bindconnect, siw_cep_alloc, siw_cm_alloc_work (failure mapped to -ENOMEM), siw_send_mpareqrep and siw_cm_queue_work; the first failure's negative errno (-ENOMEM for siw_cep_alloc, -ENOMEM for work allocation) is returned. siw_cep_alloc is the only step that allocates the CEP: before it succeeds the failure path releases the socket if one was created (sock_release) and drops the QP reference; after it succeeds the CEP is associated with the QP (qp->cep, cep->qp, taking cep and qp references) and with id (id->add_ref, cep->cm_id = id), and a failure then calls siw_socket_disassoc(s) and sock_release(s), clears cep->qp, cep->cm_id (calling id->rem_ref) and qp->cep, puts the CEP, sets cep->state = SIW_EPSTATE_CLOSED, calls siw_cep_set_free_and_put, drops the QP reference and returns the error. On success it returns 0 with the CEP in state SIW_EPSTATE_AWAIT_MPAREP, the MPA request sent, the MPA timeout work queued (siw_cm_queue_work(cep, SIW_CM_WORK_MPATIMEOUT) returned 0), the CEP freed from use with siw_cep_set_free, and the lookup's QP reference and the id reference kept by the CEP. mpa_version (module parameter) is lowered to MPA_REVISION_2 if it was larger.
note: Reviewers: round 2 (omits negative returns from siw_send_mpareqrep and siw_cm_queue_work) right: siw_send_mpareqrep returns a negative errno from kernel_sendmsg (siw_cm.c:500-502) and siw_cm_queue_work returns -ENOMEM; both now covered. Round 15 (socket not released when failure is before CEP allocation because cleanup is guarded by if (cep)): wrong, the cleanup is 'if (cep) {...} else if (s) { sock_release(s); }' (siw_cm.c error label), so the socket is released. Old claims that the caller must release the id reference and that the pre-checks have to hold on entry removed (the function checks them and the CEP keeps the references).

name: siw_qp_sq_process
prose: Precondition: qp is a valid siw_qp whose tx_wqe holds the current send WQE; the function's header comment requires the QP state read-locked; qp->sq_lock must not be held because the function takes it with spin_lock_irqsave. Postcondition: loops over WQEs: at the top of each iteration, if qp->tx_ctx.tx_suspend is set it returns the current rv (0 on the first iteration, but the positive value returned by siw_activate_tx if the iteration was re-entered after it returned a positive value). Otherwise tx_type <= SIW_OP_READ_RESPONSE goes to siw_qp_sq_proc_tx, else siw_qp_sq_proc_local. If that returns 0: for SIW_OP_SEND, _SEND_REMOTE_INV and _WRITE the memory references are released (siw_wqe_put_mem) and then, together with SIW_OP_INVAL_STAG and SIW_OP_REG_MR, a signalled WQE is completed with SIW_WC_SUCCESS; SIW_OP_READ and _READ_LOCAL_INV complete nothing here; SIW_OP_READ_RESPONSE releases its memory; any other type (including SIW_OP_SEND_WITH_IMM) warns, sets rv = -EINVAL and returns without changing wr_status. Otherwise it sets wr_status = SIW_WR_IDLE and calls siw_activate_tx under qp->sq_lock; rv <= 0 (including a negative errno from siw_activate_tx) returns that rv, rv > 0 loops. If processing returned -EAGAIN it returns 0 (paused); -EINPROGRESS returns siw_sq_start(qp) (0, or -EIO if no tx cpu is available). On any other error: under sq_lock a READ/READ_LOCAL_INV with nonzero orq_size has its ORQ entry rolled back; if tx_suspend is clear it calls siw_qp_cm_drop(qp, 0); for SEND, SEND_REMOTE_INV, SEND_WITH_IMM, WRITE, READ and READ_LOCAL_INV memory is released then (also for INVAL_STAG and REG_MR) the WQE is completed with SIW_WC_LOC_QP_OP_ERR and IB_EVENT_QP_FATAL is raised; for SIW_OP_READ_RESPONSE it raises IB_EVENT_QP_REQ_ERR and releases the memory without a completion; any other type warns and sets rv = -EINVAL; wr_status is set to SIW_WR_IDLE and it returns the error (the original rv except -EINVAL for an undefined type).
note: slice cut the head (real function at siw_qp_tx.c:997). Reviewers: round 1 (-EINPROGRESS returns siw_sq_start(qp), not -EINPROGRESS): right, old prose already said so. Round 2 (precondition wrong, siw_sq_resume holds qp->state_lock): right, the header comment says 'Must be called with the QP state read-locked'. Round 15 (returns rv which may be negative when siw_activate_tx returns <= 0): right: siw_activate_tx_from_sq can return -EINVAL (siw_qp.c:869-897); also a positive rv can be returned if tx_suspend is seen at the top of a later iteration.

name: siw_post_receive
prose: Precondition: base_qp is the ib_qp embedded in a siw_qp, wr is NULL or a NULL-terminated chain of receive work requests, and bad_wr is a writable pointer (siw_rq_flush_wr tolerates NULL). Postcondition: returns -EINVAL with *bad_wr = wr if the QP has an SRQ or rq_size is 0, or if the QP is not a kernel QP (rdma_is_kernel_res false). It then tries qp->state_lock for read without blocking: if the trylock fails and qp->attrs.state is SIW_QP_STATE_ERROR it returns siw_rq_flush_wr(qp, wr, bad_wr); if it fails in any other state it sets *bad_wr = wr and returns -ENOTCONN. With the read lock held, if qp->attrs.state is greater than SIW_QP_STATE_RTS it returns siw_rq_flush_wr(...) when the state is SIW_QP_STATE_ERROR, else sets *bad_wr = wr and returns -ENOTCONN, releasing the read lock before returning. siw_rq_flush_wr completes each WR with SIW_WC_WR_FLUSH_ERR on the CQ and, if a completion fails, sets *bad_wr (if non-NULL) to that WR and returns the error; it returns 0 if all were flushed and does not post them. Otherwise it takes qp->rq_lock (irqsave) and for each WR writes it into the receive queue slot at rq_put % rq_size and publishes it with a write barrier then SIW_WQE_VALID, advancing rq_put; the loop stops with -ENOMEM if the slot is still marked valid (queue full) or -EINVAL if wr->num_sge exceeds rq_max_sges. It then releases rq_lock and the state read lock; on a negative rv it sets *bad_wr to the WR that stopped the loop (earlier WRs of the chain stay posted). Returns 0 when the whole chain (possibly empty) was posted.
note: slice cut the head and the packet name is wrong: the real function is siw_post_receive (siw_verbs.c:1003-1113 area), there is no siw_post_recv. The old text assigned *bad_wr on all error paths; in the flush paths *bad_wr is set only by siw_rq_flush_wr when a flush completion fails.

name: ipoib_cm_req_handler
prose: Precondition: cm_id->context is the net_device of an initialized IPoIB device and the event is an incoming REQ. Postcondition: returns -ENOMEM immediately if kzalloc of the ipoib_cm_rx fails, in which case cm_id->context is unchanged and nothing else has been done. Otherwise it stores the new rx in cm_id->context (state IPOIB_CM_RX_LIVE) and creates the receive QP: if ipoib_cm_create_rx_qp fails it frees the rx and returns PTR_ERR of the QP. It then modifies the QP (error returned), and for a device without SRQ calls ipoib_cm_nonsrq_init_rx (its error is returned: -ENOMEM, -EIO if a receive post failed, or -EINVAL after it sent a CM REJ because the non-SRQ connection limit was reached); on a modify or non-SRQ-init failure it destroys the QP and frees the rx. On every failure after the first it leaves cm_id->context pointing at the freed rx. On success it queues priv->cm.stale_task after IPOIB_CM_RX_DELAY and, under priv->lock, moves the rx to priv->cm.passive_ids only if p->state is still IPOIB_CM_RX_LIVE, then calls ipoib_cm_send_rep; if the REP send fails it only warns and tries to move the QP to the error state (warning on failure), and the function returns 0 either way.
note: Reviewers: original (success may return 0 without adding to passive_ids if state changed) right, kept. Round 2 (omits -EIO from non-SRQ post_receive failure) right (ipoib_cm_nonsrq_init_rx maps the post failure to -EIO). Round 15 (kzalloc failure returns -ENOMEM before cm_id->context is set; no QP destroy or rx free) right: old prose implied destroy/free on that path.

name: ipoib_tx_poll
prose: Precondition: napi is the send_napi member of a valid ipoib_dev_priv whose send_cq and send_wc are usable; budget is the NAPI budget. Postcondition: polls up to MAX_SEND_CQE completions from priv->send_cq into priv->send_wc with ib_poll_cq; for each polled wc it calls ipoib_cm_handle_tx_wc if wr_id has IPOIB_OP_CM set, else ipoib_ib_handle_tx_wc (a negative ib_poll_cq result processes no completions). If n < budget (this includes a negative n) it calls napi_complete and then ib_req_notify_cq(send_cq, IB_CQ_NEXT_COMP | IB_CQ_REPORT_MISSED_EVENTS); if that returns nonzero and napi_schedule(napi) returns true it polls again from the top. Returns n, or 0 if n is negative.
note: slice cut the head and the packet name is invented: the real function is ipoib_tx_poll (ipoib_ib.c:499). The old claim that it leaves no locks, references or memory held was removed (not tied to a line); the old text 'if that reports missed events' is replaced by 'returns nonzero' as the code tests the return value of ib_req_notify_cq only for non-zero.

name: neigh_add_path
prose: Precondition: skb is an outgoing IPoIB unicast packet, daddr is the destination hardware address taken from its pseudo header, dev is the IPoIB net device, and the caller does not hold priv->lock. Postcondition: takes priv->lock with spin_lock_irqsave and releases it on every return path. It calls ipoib_neigh_alloc, which returns a new or existing neighbour holding a reference for the caller, or NULL. If it returns NULL, tx_dropped is incremented, the skb is freed and NULL is returned. If the neighbour's list is already non-empty (already added to a path by someone else) it unlocks and returns that neighbour, with the skb not consumed and the caller owning the reference. Otherwise it finds or creates the path for daddr + 4 (creation failure goes to err_path), adds the neighbour to the path's neigh_list, and then: if path->ah is valid it takes a kref on it and sets neigh->ah; with CM enabled for the neighbour it creates the CM tx if none exists (failure: ipoib_neigh_free then drop), and queues the skb (after push_pseudo_header) on neigh->queue if its length is below IPOIB_MAX_PATH_REC_QUEUE, else drops it; without CM it unlocks and sends the skb with rn->send, stores the result in path->ah->last_send, drops the neighbour reference and returns NULL. If path->ah is not valid it sets neigh->ah to NULL, calls path_rec_start if no query is pending (failure: ipoib_neigh_free then drop), and queues the skb on neigh->queue if under the limit, else drops it. A drop increments dev->stats.tx_dropped and frees the skb; after queueing or dropping it unlocks, drops the neighbour reference and returns NULL.
note: slice cut the head (real function at ipoib_main.c:989). Reviewers: original (function acquires the lock and allocates the neighbour) right. Round 2 (all code paths return NULL): wrong, the 'if (unlikely(!list_empty(&neigh->list)))' path returns the neighbour (ipoib_main.c:1360-1363) and the caller ipoib_start_xmit continues with it. Round 15 (queues only on neigh->queue, not a path queue): right, old prose wrongly said path's queue.

name: ipoib_mcast_join_task
prose: Precondition: work is the mcast_task.work member of a valid ipoib_dev_priv; the caller does not hold priv->lock. Postcondition: returns void. It returns without changing state if ipoib_mcast_allowed is false, ib_query_port fails, or the port state is not IB_PORT_ACTIVE. Otherwise it stores port_attr.lid in priv->local_lid, and, under netif_addr_lock_bh, returns if IPOIB_FLAG_DEV_ADDR_SET is clear (local_lid has already been written). It then takes priv->lock with spin_lock_irq and, if ipoib_mcast_allowed is now false, goes to out. If priv->broadcast is NULL it allocates a group: on failure it schedules the join thread with a 1 second delay and goes to out; otherwise it copies the broadcast GID into it, stores it in priv->broadcast and adds it with __ipoib_mcast_add. If the broadcast group is not attached (IPOIB_MCAST_FLAG_ATTACHED clear) it selects it for joining when its mc is NULL or an error and it is not busy, except that when its backoff is above 1 and delay_until has not yet passed it is not selected and delay_until is recorded instead; then it goes to out. Otherwise it walks priv->multicast_list: for each group with mc unset/error, not busy, and either not send-only or with queued packets, if backoff is 1 or delay_until has passed it calls ipoib_mcast_join (if that returns nonzero it unlocks and returns at once), else it records the earliest delay_until. After a complete walk no group is selected. At out it cancels and requeues mcast_task at the recorded delay_until if one was recorded, calls ipoib_mcast_join on the selected group if any (its result ignored), and releases priv->lock.
note: slice contains the function head. Reviewers: original (prose claims all unjoined groups join) right/fixed earlier; round 2 (local_lid written before DEV_ADDR_SET check) right (ipoib_multicast.c:1460), prose says so; round 15 (broadcast group with backoff > 1 is selected once delay_until passes): right, the old prose omitted the 'time_before(jiffies, delay_until)' condition for deselecting.

name: isert_rdma_rw_ctx_post
prose: Precondition: cmd, conn and cmd->iscsit_cmd are valid; conn->cm_id is valid (its port_num is read unconditionally on entry); conn->qp is valid. If cmd->ctx_init_done is false the se_cmd scatterlists (and protection scatterlists when isert_prot_cmd(conn, se_cmd) is true) and the remote key/address for the transfer direction (cmd->write_stag/write_va with offset cmd->iscsit_cmd->write_data_done for DMA_FROM_DEVICE, else cmd->read_stag/read_va with offset 0) are valid; if it is true, cmd->rw was initialized by an earlier call. Postcondition: if ctx_init_done is false, it first initializes cmd->rw with rdma_rw_ctx_signature_init (after isert_set_sig_attrs) when the command has protection information, else with rdma_rw_ctx_init; a negative result (isert_set_sig_attrs can only fail with -EINVAL) is returned before anything is posted and ctx_init_done stays false (a positive return from rdma_rw_ctx_init is treated as success and discarded); on success it sets ctx_init_done to true. It then calls rdma_rw_ctx_post(&cmd->rw, conn->qp, port_num, cqe, chain_wr) and returns its result (0 or negative errno from ib_post_send); if that fails ctx_init_done stays true, cmd->rw stays initialized, and an error is logged. cqe and chain_wr are passed through unchanged; chain_wr, if non-NULL, is appended after the RDMA work requests by rdma_rw_ctx_post.
note: the packet name isert_rdma_rw_ctx_init_or_post is invented: the real function is isert_rdma_rw_ctx_post (ib_isert.c:2087). Reviewers: round 1 (ctx_init_done stays true after post failure) right; round 2 (conn->cm_id->port_num dereferenced unconditionally) right (initializer of port_num); round 15 (chain_wr is chained after the RDMA WRs, cqe may be NULL) right on the chaining; rdma_rw_ctx_post's comment says cqe must be set when chain_wr is NULL.

name: opa_vnic_vema_send_trap
prose: Precondition: adapter is a valid opa_vnic_adapter and data points to a valid __opa_veswport_trap; lid is the issuer LID; no lock is held. Postcondition: returns void. It jumps to err_exit (which only logs 'Aborting trap', with nothing to release) if adapter->cport is NULL, vema_get_port(cport, data->opaportnum) returns NULL or a port without mad_agent, the trap rate limit is hit (jiffies before adapter->trap_timeout and trap_count already OPA_VNIC_TRAP_BURST_LIMIT, after logging 'Trap rate exceeded'), or class->trap_lid is 0. The rate counter is updated before the later steps: within the timeout window trap_count is incremented, otherwise it is reset to 0, so it changes even if a later step fails. Otherwise it builds an address handle with rdma_create_ah (failure logs and goes to err_exit), finds the full default pkey index (falling back to the partial default pkey, then to index 1), and allocates a send MAD with ib_create_send_mad (failure: destroys the address handle with rdma_destroy_ah then err_exit). It fills the MAD header and OUI, increments port->tid, sets issuer_lid from lid and copies the byte-swapped trap fields from data. It posts with ib_post_send_mad: on failure it frees the send MAD, destroys the AH and logs 'Aborting trap'; on success it hands the send buffer and AH to the MAD layer and, if adapter->trap_count is 0, sets adapter->trap_timeout to jiffies + usecs_to_jiffies(OPA_VNIC_TRAP_TIMEOUT), then returns.
note: slice cut the head and the packet name is unnamed: the real function is opa_vnic_vema_send_trap (opa_vnic_vema.c:709-852 region). The old prose omitted the early err_exit returns (NULL cport / port / mad_agent and rate limit) and the pre-AH trap_count update.

name: srp_rport_reconnect
prose: Precondition: calls are serialized by the caller and no srp_queuecommand, srp_abort, srp_reset_device or srp_reset_host runs concurrently; rport->lld_data is a valid srp_target_port. Postcondition: it calls srp_disconnect_target(target) first; if target->state is SRP_TARGET_SCANNING it returns -ENODEV and does nothing else. Otherwise it calls srp_new_cm_id for each channel and sums the return values in ret; then scsi_host_busy_iter with srp_terminate_cmd (scsi_result DID_RESET << 16); then, for each channel, srp_create_ch_ib (its result added to ret) and re-initialization of ch->free_tx with the queue_size tx_ring entries; then sets target->qp_in_error = false unconditionally (even if ret is nonzero); then calls srp_connect_ch for the channels in order (multich false for the first, true after), stopping before any channel once ret is nonzero. If ret is 0 it prints 'reconnect succeeded'. Returns ret: 0, the sum of the srp_new_cm_id and srp_create_ch_ib results if any was nonzero (no srp_connect_ch call is made then), or the first nonzero srp_connect_ch result; on failure the channels can be left partially recreated.
note: Reviewers: original (qp_in_error cleared unconditionally including when ret != 0) right, as written in the old prose and kept. Round 15 (code calls srp_new_cm_id first, not busy-command iteration): right, old prose order was wrong; corrected to srp_new_cm_id loop, then scsi_host_busy_iter, then create loop.

name: srp_ib_cm_rej_handler
prose: Precondition: event is an IB CM REJ event for ch. For IB_CM_REJ_PORT_CM_REDIRECT, event->param.rej_rcvd.ari must point to a valid struct ib_class_port_info; for IB_CM_REJ_PORT_REDIRECT on a Topspin target it must point to at least 16 bytes; for IB_CM_REJ_CONSUMER_DEFINED, event->private_data must point to a readable opcode byte and, when that opcode is SRP_LOGIN_REJ, to a valid struct srp_login_rej. Postcondition: returns void; ch->status is assigned exactly once in every switch case including default, never left unassigned. IB_CM_REJ_PORT_CM_REDIRECT: ch->ib_cm.path dlid, pkey and dgid and cm_id->remote_cm_qpn are updated from the class port info (in both sub-cases) and ch->status = SRP_DLID_REDIRECT if the redirect LID is nonzero else SRP_PORT_REDIRECT. IB_CM_REJ_PORT_REDIRECT: on a Topspin target ch->ib_cm.path.dgid is overwritten with the 16 bytes at ari and status is SRP_PORT_REDIRECT, otherwise status is -ECONNRESET. IB_CM_REJ_STALE_CONN: status SRP_STALE_CONN. IB_CM_REJ_DUPLICATE_LOCAL_COMM_ID, IB_CM_REJ_CONSUMER_DEFINED (with a warning log of the login-reject reason or opcode) and any other reason: status -ECONNRESET. It allocates no memory and logs through shost_printk.
note: Reviewers: original and round 15 (does not set ch->status for unhandled reasons / default and STALE_CONN absent): wrong, the default case sets ch->status = -ECONNRESET and IB_CM_REJ_STALE_CONN sets SRP_STALE_CONN (ib_srp.c switch). Round 2 (omits private_data and ari validity preconditions) right, now stated. Old prose said dlid/pkey/dgid updated only for the nonzero-LID case; the code updates them in both cases.

name: evdev_write
prose: Precondition: file->private_data is an evdev_client with a valid evdev; buffer is a user pointer readable for count bytes. Postcondition: count is first clamped to min(count, 4096). Returns -EINVAL if the clamped count is nonzero but smaller than input_event_size(); returns the error from mutex_lock_interruptible(&evdev->mutex) if interrupted (before any event is read); returns -ENODEV if evdev->exist is false or client->revoked is set. Otherwise it repeatedly reads one input_event from user space and calls input_inject_event for it while a whole event remains within the clamped count; if input_event_from_user fails it returns -EFAULT (events already injected stay injected). On normal completion it returns the number of bytes consumed, a multiple of input_event_size() not above min(count, 4096) (any trailing partial event is ignored), and 0 for count 0. evdev->mutex is released on every path after it was acquired.
note: slice cut the head (real function at evdev.c:498). Reviewer round 15 (code does not clamp count to 4096): wrong, 'count = min(count, 4096);' is in the function body (before the -EINVAL check).

name: input_get_disposition
prose: Precondition: dev is an initialized input_dev; pval points to a readable and writable int holding the event value. Postcondition: if dev->inhibited it returns INPUT_IGNORE_EVENT without changing any state and without writing *pval. Otherwise the value is read from *pval, a disposition is chosen by event type and code, and the possibly updated value (changed only by the EV_ABS defuzz/slot logic) is written back to *pval before returning. EV_SYN: SYN_CONFIG gives INPUT_PASS_TO_ALL, SYN_REPORT gives INPUT_PASS_TO_HANDLERS | INPUT_FLUSH, SYN_MT_REPORT gives INPUT_PASS_TO_HANDLERS, other codes ignore. EV_KEY (supported code): value 2 gives INPUT_PASS_TO_HANDLERS without changing dev->key; otherwise if the bit in dev->key differs from !!value it is toggled and INPUT_PASS_TO_HANDLERS is returned; else ignore. EV_SW (supported code): if the dev->sw bit differs from !!value it is toggled and INPUT_PASS_TO_HANDLERS returned, else ignore. EV_ABS (supported code): input_handle_abs_event decides: ABS_MT_SLOT only stages the slot (INPUT_IGNORE_EVENT), an event whose defuzzed value equals the old value is ignored, otherwise INPUT_PASS_TO_HANDLERS (| INPUT_SLOT when a pending new slot is flushed). EV_REL (supported code): INPUT_PASS_TO_HANDLERS if value is nonzero. EV_MSC (supported code): INPUT_PASS_TO_ALL. EV_LED (supported code): if the dev->led bit differs from !!value it is toggled and INPUT_PASS_TO_ALL returned, else ignore. EV_SND (supported code): the dev->snd bit is toggled if it differs from !!value, and INPUT_PASS_TO_ALL is returned either way. EV_REP: if code <= REP_MAX, value >= 0 and dev->rep[code] != value, dev->rep[code] is set and INPUT_PASS_TO_ALL returned, else ignore. EV_FF: INPUT_PASS_TO_ALL if value >= 0. EV_PWR: INPUT_PASS_TO_ALL. Any unsupported code or unknown type returns INPUT_IGNORE_EVENT.
note: Reviewers: original (EV_KEY value 2 passes to handlers with state unchanged) right, kept. Round 2 (EV_REL/ABS/MSC require supported code, REL nonzero; EV_PWR returns PASS_TO_ALL, not ignore) right. Round 15 (inhibited path does not write *pval; ABS_MT_SLOT returns IGNORE) right on both: old prose said it writes *pval in all cases and passed every supported ABS event to handlers.

name: joydump_connect
prose: Precondition: gameport is a valid gameport and drv is the driver connecting to it. Postcondition: it logs a header, then tries gameport_open in GAMEPORT_MODE_RAW; if that fails it logs, tries GAMEPORT_MODE_COOKED, and if that also fails it logs and returns -ENODEV (no mode open). If the cooked open succeeded it prints the cooked axes and buttons and a footer, and then continues exactly as on the raw path. It computes a 10 ms timeout and allocates a BUF_SIZE (256) entry buffer; if the allocation fails it logs 'no memory for testing' and goes to the footer. Otherwise it records an initial sample at time 0, triggers the gameport, and with local interrupts disabled samples gameport_read until the buffer holds BUF_SIZE entries or the timeout is reached, storing an entry whenever the data changes (the buffer holds the initial sample plus at most 255 transitions); then it prints the table of samples with time deltas, frees the buffer and prints the footer. Every path other than the -ENODEV one returns 0 with the gameport left open (it is closed by the disconnect handler); the buffer is freed only on the path that allocated it.
note: Reviewers: original (omits kmalloc failure path returning 0) and round 2 right, now covered. Round 1 (after allocation failure with cooked fallback the cooked reading was already printed) right. Round 15 (buffer holds the initial sample plus at most 255 transitions, not 256 transitions) right (BUF_SIZE 256, i starts at 1, loop i < BUF_SIZE). The old prose claimed no dump is sampled after a cooked fallback; the code goes on to sample and dump in both modes.

name: imx_keypad_check_for_events
prose: Precondition: invoked as the check_matrix_timer callback of an initialized imx_keypad (keypad->mmio_base mapped, clock enabled, masks and state arrays initialized); the function itself does not test whether the keypad is enabled or open. Postcondition: returns void. It scans the matrix into a local zeroed array with imx_keypad_scan_matrix, then compares, only over columns set in keypad->cols_en_mask, the new scan with keypad->matrix_unstable_state; if any of those columns differs it copies the whole scan into matrix_unstable_state and sets stable_count = 0, otherwise it increments stable_count. If stable_count is below IMX_KEYPAD_SCANS_FOR_STABILITY it re-arms the timer for 10 ms and returns without reporting events and without touching KPSR. If stable_count equals the threshold it reports key changes with imx_keypad_fire_events and copies the scan into matrix_stable_state (a larger count reports nothing). It then checks whether all columns of the scan (not only enabled ones) are zero: if so it sets KBD_STAT_KPKD | KBD_STAT_KDSC in KPSR, then sets KBD_STAT_KDIE and clears KBD_STAT_KRIE, and does not re-arm the timer; otherwise it re-arms the timer for 60 ms, sets KBD_STAT_KPKR | KBD_STAT_KRSS and then sets KBD_STAT_KRIE and clears KBD_STAT_KDIE.
note: slice cut the head (real function at imx_keypad.c:181). Reviewers: original (KDI enabled when all keys released, KRI for pressed keys) right, matches prose. Round 2 (omits early return when keypad disabled): wrong, there is no such check in the function. Round 15 (updates only first differing column, compares all columns): wrong, the loop breaks at the first differing enabled column only to set state_changed, the memcpy copies the whole array, and columns outside cols_en_mask are skipped (imx_keypad.c 'continue' on cols_en_mask).

name: da7280_haptics_upload_effect
prose: Precondition: dev has a valid da7280_haptic as drvdata; effect points to a valid ff_effect, and for FF_PERIODIC effect->u.periodic.custom_data is a user pointer readable for custom_len s16 values; old is unused. Postcondition: returns -EBUSY if haptics->active is set. FF_CONSTANT: sets op_mode = const_op_mode; in DA7280_DRO_MODE sets level = (constant.level * 254) / 0x7FFF, otherwise sets gain = constant.level, or 0 when level <= 0; no register write; returns 0. FF_PERIODIC: returns -EINVAL if the waveform is not FF_CUSTOM. If custom_len == DA7280_CUSTOM_DATA_LEN it copies the data (-EFAULT on failure), returns -EINVAL if the sequence id or loop is outside 0..DA7280_SEQ_ID_MAX / 0..DA7280_SEQ_LOOP_MAX, then sets ps_seq_id and ps_seq_loop (low 4 bits), op_mode = periodic_op_mode and writes DA7280_SEQ_CTL2 with regmap_write (returning its error). If custom_len == DA7280_CUSTOM_GP_DATA_LEN it copies the data (-EFAULT on failure), returns -EINVAL if the GPI sequence id is outside 0..DA7280_SEQ_ID_MAX or the GPI number is outside 0..DA7280_GPI_SEQ_ID_MAX, then sets gpi_ctl[num].seq_id, op_mode = periodic_op_mode and updates DA7280_GPI_0_CTL + num with regmap_update_bits (returning its error). Otherwise custom_len must lie in (DA7280_CUSTOM_DATA_LEN, DA7280_SNP_MEM_SIZE], else -EINVAL; it copies the data (-EFAULT on failure), zeroes haptics->snp_mem, fills it one byte per sample (returning -EINVAL as soon as a sample is outside 0..0xff, leaving snp_mem partly filled), and calls da7280_haptic_mem_update, returning its error if nonzero; this branch does not change op_mode. Any other effect type returns -EINVAL. Returns 0 on success. When a register write fails, the fields already assigned in haptics (op_mode, ps_seq_id, ps_seq_loop, gpi_ctl[num].seq_id) stay modified.
note: slice cut the head and the packet name is wrong: the real function is da7280_haptics_upload_effect (da7280.c:504). Old prose wrongly said the active flag is a precondition (the function checks it and returns -EBUSY) and that op_mode is set in the waveform memory branch (it is not).

name: copy_keymap
prose: Precondition: the global keymap points to an array of struct key_entry terminated by an entry whose type is KE_END. Postcondition: counts the entries up to and including the KE_END terminator, duplicates that many entries with kmemdup_array(GFP_KERNEL) and, on success, stores the copy in the global keymap and returns 0; if the allocation fails it returns -ENOMEM and keymap is left unchanged. The original array is not freed here.
note: Old contract removed (the function reads and writes the global keymap). Reviewer round 15 (contract omits ENOMEM) is moot since the contract is now empty.

name: select_keymap
prose: Precondition: module parameters keymap_name and force and the dmi_ids table are initialized; the global keymap is NULL or points to a valid keymap. Postcondition: calls dmi_check_system(dmi_ids), which may set the global keymap. If keymap_name is non-NULL it sets keymap to the table named '1557/MS2141', 'aopen1557', 'prestigio' or 'generic', overriding a DMI choice; for any other name it logs and returns -EINVAL without calling copy_keymap. If keymap is still NULL afterwards it returns -ENODEV (after logging) when force is false, or sets keymap to keymap_empty when force is true. It then returns copy_keymap(): 0 with keymap replaced by a heap copy of the selected table, or -ENOMEM if that allocation fails, in which case keymap stays pointing at the selected static table.
note: Old contract removed (reads and writes globals). Old prose said keymap is 'unchanged' on -ENOMEM; it remains the selected static table (assigned earlier in this function), and the -EINVAL/-ENODEV paths do not clear a keymap that DMI may have set.

name: rmi_f11_get_query_parameters
prose: Precondition: rmi_dev is a valid RMI device, f11 and sensor_query are valid, f11->has_query9, has_query11, has_query12, has_query27 and has_query28 have already been set from earlier reads, and query_base_addr is the base of the F11 query registers. Postcondition: it reads RMI_F11_QUERY_SIZE bytes at query_base_addr (a negative result is returned at once) and fills nr_fingers, has_rel, has_abs, has_gestures, has_sensitivity_adjust, configurable and the electrode counts from them; has_abs and has_rel here come from this first read, not from earlier calls. It then reads further query registers at increasing offsets: one byte if has_abs, one byte if has_rel, RMI_F11_QUERY_GESTURE_SIZE bytes if has_gestures, and one byte each if f11->has_query9, has_touch_shapes (set by this function), f11->has_query11, f11->has_query12, has_jitter_filter, has_info2; a block of 4 bytes when has_physical_props (advancing the offset by 12); skipping one byte if f11->has_query27; and one byte if f11->has_query28, and, if its bit 6 is set, advancing the offset by 2 and reading one more byte, setting f11->has_acm when bit 5 is set. Any failed read returns that negative error at once with sensor_query only partly filled. On success it returns query_size, the running byte offset past the query registers it accounted for (at least RMI_F11_QUERY_SIZE).
note: slice cut the head and the packet name is wrong: the real function is rmi_f11_get_query_parameters (rmi_f11.c:786). Old prose said has_abs, has_rel and has_gestures were populated from earlier reads; they are set from the first block read inside this function. query_size is an offset (a count of bytes accounted for), not strictly bytes read: skipped query27 and the 12-byte physical-props span are added without being read.

name: __ps2_command
prose: Precondition: the caller serializes calls (the function takes no command mutex; callers use ps2_begin_command/ps2_end_command). param is NULL or points to a buffer of at least max(send, receive) bytes, where send = (command >> 12) & 0xf and receive = (command >> 8) & 0xf. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL with WARN_ON(1), before any state change, if receive exceeds sizeof(ps2dev->cmdbuf) or if send is nonzero and param is NULL. Otherwise it copies the send bytes, pauses serio rx, sets cmdcnt = receive and the flags for the command (PS2_FLAG_WAITID for GETID; PS2_FLAG_PASS_NOACK for SETLEDS, EX_SETLEDS, SETREP; PS2_FLAG_CMD | PS2_FLAG_CMD1 added when receive > 0), preloading cmdbuf from param in reverse order when param is non-NULL. It sends the command byte (timeout 1000 for RESET_BAT, else 200) and the send parameter bytes with ps2_do_sendbyte; the first failure sets rc to its error and skips the response wait and the copy-out (param is unchanged). Otherwise it waits (up to 500 ms, 4000 ms for RESET_BAT, plus ps2_adjust_timeout) for the response, and if param is non-NULL copies receive bytes from cmdbuf into param in reverse order; if ps2dev->cmdcnt is still nonzero it sets rc = -EPROTO unless the command is PS2_CMD_RESET_BAT with exactly one byte missing (in which case rc is 0); with this -EPROTO result param has already been overwritten from cmdbuf. On every path after the pause, ps2dev->flags is set to 0 and rx is resumed. Returns rc, with -EAGAIN converted to -EPROTO: 0, the ps2_do_sendbyte error (other than -EAGAIN), or -EPROTO. If param is NULL and receive > 0 the response is not copied out and remains in ps2dev->cmdbuf.
note: slice cut the head (real function at libps2.c:251). Reviewers: original (response not copied when param is NULL) right, prose says so. Round 2 (send failures return the underlying rc except -EAGAIN, not -EPROTO) right and the prose matches (-EAGAIN becomes -EPROTO at the final return). Old claim that param may hold partial data on any failure corrected: on send failure param is untouched.

name: ps2_handle_ack
prose: Precondition: called from the serio receive path on a byte received from the device (no locks are taken here); ps2dev->receive_handler is valid when PS2_FLAG_PASS_NOACK can be set. Postcondition: returns void. PS2_RET_ACK sets ps2dev->nak = 0. PS2_RET_NAK sets PS2_FLAG_NAK and nak = PS2_RET_NAK. PS2_RET_ERR with PS2_FLAG_NAK set clears that flag and sets nak = PS2_RET_ERR. PS2_RET_ERR without PS2_FLAG_NAK, or 0x00, 0x03 or 0x04, with PS2_FLAG_WAITID set sets nak = 0 (PS2_FLAG_WAITID is left set). Those cases then continue to a common tail which clears PS2_FLAG_NAK if nak is 0, clears PS2_FLAG_ACK, and calls ps2_handle_response(ps2dev, data) if nak is 0 and data is not PS2_RET_ACK, otherwise wakes ps2dev->wait; so ACK, NAK, and ERR-after-NAK wake the waiter and the WAITID/ERR-without-NAK case passes data to ps2_handle_response. Any other byte, including PS2_RET_ERR without NAK or 0x00/0x03/0x04 without WAITID, takes the default branch: it logs, calls ps2dev->receive_handler(ps2dev, data) if PS2_FLAG_PASS_NOACK is set, clears PS2_FLAG_WAITID and PS2_FLAG_PASS_NOACK, and returns without touching nak, PS2_FLAG_NAK, PS2_FLAG_ACK or the wait queue.
note: Reviewers: original (PS2_FLAG_NAK is cleared on ERR after NAK, so it does not track whether a NAK was seen) right: it is cleared on ERR after NAK and kept set after NAK; round 2 (ACK does not clear it, so it can persist) wrong: after ACK nak is 0 so the tail clears PS2_FLAG_NAK (the 'if (!ps2dev->nak) flags &= ~PS2_FLAG_NAK' line). Old prose wrongly sent PS2_RET_ERR without NAK straight to ps2_handle_response; it does so only if PS2_FLAG_WAITID is set, otherwise it takes the default branch.

name: mxt_check_bootloader
prose: Precondition: data is a valid mxt_data with an initialized bl_completion and bootloader address; state is the expected bootloader status; if wait is true the CHG interrupt completes bl_completion. Postcondition: if wait is true it waits on bl_completion for up to MXT_FW_CHG_TIMEOUT (300 ms) before each read; a nonzero result (-ETIMEDOUT, or a negative error from an interrupted wait) is returned after a log. It then reads one status byte with mxt_bootloader_read (nonzero error returned). If state is MXT_WAITING_BOOTLOAD_CMD the byte is replaced by mxt_get_bootloader_version(data, val): if the byte has MXT_BOOT_EXTENDED_ID set and a fresh 3-byte read succeeds, the result is the first byte of that fresh read (buf[0]); if that read fails the original byte is kept (the failure is only logged); without the bit the original byte is kept. For MXT_WAITING_BOOTLOAD_CMD, MXT_WAITING_FRAME_DATA and MXT_APP_CRC_FAIL the byte is then masked with ~MXT_BOOT_STATUS_MASK; for MXT_FRAME_CRC_PASS the byte is not masked: if it equals MXT_FRAME_CRC_CHECK the wait/read starts again, if it equals MXT_FRAME_CRC_FAIL it returns -EINVAL; for any other state it returns -EINVAL after the read. Finally it returns -EINVAL if the byte differs from state, else 0. No device state is written.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (MXT_FRAME_CRC_PASS is not masked) right. Round 2 (omits mxt_get_bootloader_version; extended-ID read failure is swallowed and value may be buf[0]) right. Round 15 (mxt_get_bootloader_version returns buf[0], the status byte, not the ID which is buf[1]) right: old prose said it returns the bootloader ID byte.

name: hp680_ts_init
prose: Precondition: module init function, takes no arguments. Postcondition: allocates the global hp680_ts_dev with input_allocate_device and returns -ENOMEM if that fails; otherwise it sets event bits, ABS_X/ABS_Y ranges, name and phys, then calls request_irq for HP680_TS_IRQ: if it returns negative it logs and returns -EBUSY after input_free_device. It then calls input_register_device: on failure it calls free_irq, cancel_delayed_work_sync(&work) and input_free_device and returns the registration error. On success it returns 0 with the IRQ requested and the device registered. The global hp680_ts_dev is not reset to NULL on failure after allocation.
note: Contract removed (the function allocates and writes globals). Reviewers on the old formal contract (weaker than prose, allows any negative return) right, so no contract is given.

name: mip4_interrupt
prose: Precondition: dev_id is a valid initialized mip4_ts whose I2C client, buffer and input device are usable. Postcondition: always returns IRQ_HANDLED (single return). It reads the packet info byte with mip4_i2c_xfer; on failure it logs and returns without input_sync. It takes size from the low 7 bits and alert from bit 7; if size is 0 it logs and returns without input_sync. It then reads size bytes of packet data into ts->buf; if that read fails it logs and returns without input_sync. If alert is set it only logs a debug message and returns without handling packets and without input_sync. Otherwise it calls mip4_handle_packet on successive ts->event_size strides until one returns an error or the data is exhausted, and then calls input_sync regardless of whether a handler failed.
note: Reviewers: original (alert packets skip packet processing and input_sync) right, and round 15 (omits packet-data read failure) right: both are covered now.

name: rohm_ts_soft_irq
prose: Precondition: dev_id is a valid rohm_ts_data whose client and input device are usable; called as the threaded IRQ handler. Postcondition: always returns IRQ_HANDLED. It writes INT_MASK = INT_ALL, then INT_CLEAR = 0xff, then burst-reads the position registers; if any of the three fails it returns at once, without reporting input, without changing ts->finger_count and without writing the final INT_MASK. Using the gesture byte masked with TOUCH_MASK: 0 touches increments ts->contact_count[0] (compared with untouch_threshold[prev finger_count]), SINGLE_TOUCH increments contact_count[1] (single_touch_threshold) and, if reached, moves a nonzero second position into the first slot, DUAL_TOUCH increments contact_count[2] (dual_touch_threshold); any other value (three or more touches) logs and returns at once without touching contact_count or finger_count and without the final INT_MASK write. If the relevant threshold is reached finger_count is set to 0, 1 or 2 and, if it differs from the previous ts->finger_count, all contact counters are zeroed except that of the new finger count; it then assigns slots, reports finger_count contacts with positions, syncs the frame and pointer emulation, calls input_sync and stores finger_count in ts->finger_count. If the threshold is not reached nothing is reported and ts->finger_count is unchanged. If the gesture byte has CALIBRATION_REQUEST set it calls rohm_ts_manual_calibration and only warns on failure. Finally it writes INT_MASK = CALIBRATION_DONE | SLEEP_OUT | SLEEP_IN | PROGRAM_LOAD_DONE and ignores the result.
note: Reviewers: original (no I2C error can still return early for 3+ touches or debounce) right, covered. Round 15 (counters are zeroed only when the finger count changes) right: the memset is under 'if (prev_finger_count != finger_count)' and preserves the new state's count; old prose said zeroed whenever the threshold is reached.

name: rohm_ts_load_firmware
prose: Precondition: client is a valid I2C client; firmware_name names a firmware image requestable from the device. Postcondition: the firmware is released automatically on return (__free(firmware)). If request_firmware fails it returns that error without any I2C write. Otherwise it writes INT_MASK (COORD_UPDATE | CALIBRATION_DONE | SLEEP_IN | SLEEP_OUT), then runs up to FIRMWARE_RETRY_MAX + 1 load attempts: each attempt (after the first, first writing EX_WDAT = 0) writes EX_ADDR_H, EX_ADDR_L and COMMON_SETUP1, sends the image to EX_WDAT in blocks of at most FIRMWARE_BLOCK_SIZE, reads INT_STATUS, writes INT_CLEAR = 0xff, and stops successfully if INT_STATUS equals PROGRAM_LOAD_DONE; otherwise the attempt ends with error -EIO and the next attempt starts. The first failing I2C operation (a register or block write, the INT_STATUS read, or the INT_CLEAR write) ends the function with that error. After the loop, success or not, it writes INT_MASK = INT_ALL. It returns the load error if nonzero (an I2C error from the failing operation, or -EIO if no attempt saw PROGRAM_LOAD_DONE), else the result of that final INT_MASK write (so a successful load can still return that write's error).
note: Reviewers: original (successful load can still return the final INT_MASK write error) right. Round 15 (INT_CLEAR failure returns that error): right, INT_CLEAR write errors goto out and are returned (the old enumeration omitted them), and the final INT_MASK error is only returned when the load error is 0.
